sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in the React tools for remembering values and loading data.
sections.why: Likely reason: needed for loading and saving settings.

sections.name: Provider
sections.title: Provider option shape
sections.what: Describes one provider option: its name, description, cost, privacy, requirements and model names.
sections.why: Likely reason: tells the page which fields to show for each card.
sections.watch_out: Must match the backend's provider response or cards will show blanks.

sections.name: SettingsData
sections.title: Saved settings shape
sections.what: Describes the saved settings: the chosen provider, whether an OpenAI key exists, and the Ollama address.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page shows the current configuration from this data.
sections.watch_out: The actual key is never stored in this data, only a yes or no.

sections.name: Settings (part 1)
sections.title: Loading settings and the save action
sections.what: Loads providers and current settings when the page opens, then sends the chosen provider and optional key to the backend on Save and shows a message.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page must show the current choice before the user changes it.
sections.watch_out: A failed save shows only the generic text Error saving settings with no reason.

sections.name: Settings (part 2)
sections.title: Provider cards
sections.what: Draws each provider as a card the user can select, showing cost, privacy, requirements and model names.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user compare options at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Clicking a card changes the selection on screen only; nothing is saved until Save is pressed.

sections.name: Settings (part 3)
sections.title: OpenAI key box and current settings panel
sections.what: Shows the key box only when OpenAI is selected, provides Save and Cancel buttons, and summarises the current configuration at the bottom.
sections.why: Likely reason: the key is needed only for OpenAI, so the box is hidden otherwise.
sections.watch_out: The key is sent in plain form on save, and the browser may remember what was typed.

summary: Settings page where the user chooses the AI provider, enters an OpenAI key if needed, and saves the choice to the backend.
purpose: Lets the user pick between a local model service and OpenAI and shows the current setup.
why: Likely reason: the backend stores the choice so the rest of the app uses it.
how: When the page opens, it loads the provider list and current settings from the backend at the same time. It shows one selectable card per provider. The OpenAI key box appears only when OpenAI is chosen. Save sends the provider and key to the backend and shows a message for three seconds. A panel at the bottom shows the current configuration.
inputs: Provider list and settings from the backend, the user's selection and the typed key.
outputs: A save request to the backend, a success or error message, and the current configuration panel.
risks: The key is held in the page's memory and sent in plain form over the local address. The saved key is never shown back, only whether one is set. A blank key is sent as undefined, so the backend must keep the old key; that behaviour is not visible here. If loading fails, the page stays mostly empty with only a console message. Cancel is a plain link that reloads the page without saving.
debug: If provider cards are missing, confirm the backend is running and the provider endpoint returns data. If Save shows an error, check the backend logs for the update endpoint. If the key seems unsaved, confirm it was typed before Save.
